operations.evidence: the CSEW is a face-to-face survey of around 31,000 people aged 16 years or over in England and Wales
the CSEW is sample-based rather than a census and is subject to sampling error
police recorded crime is a full count of notifiable crimes reported to and recorded by the police
the count excludes crimes not reported or not recorded and is not a full count of all crime
Crime in England and Wales statistics are produced quarterly
quarterly statistics are not a live incident feed
CSEW respondents are asked about crime experiences in the 12 months before interview
the retrospective reference period introduces recall and telescoping risks
the CSEW excludes crimes against businesses, people not resident in households, homicide and victimless offences such as drug possession
CSEW estimates cannot be used as a complete count of all crime or all populations
the provisional CSEW response rate for the year ending March 2026 was 48%
the response rate is below historical levels and the published quality review should accompany use
CSEW estimates provide long-term trend information from the year ending December 1981 to the year ending March 2026
long-term comparisons must retain documented survey scope and methodology changes
police recorded crime figures are supplied from 43 territorial police forces plus British Transport Police
force-area coverage does not identify the exact site of an offence
police recorded crime coverage is defined by the Notifiable Offence List and excludes non-notifiable offences such as anti-social behaviour and parking offences
police recorded crime totals should not be presented as covering all police incidents
police recorded crime data do not currently meet the required standard for accredited official statistics because of recording quality and consistency concerns
the data require explicit recording-practice caveats and should not be treated as error-free
CSEW and police recorded crime together provide a more comprehensive picture than either source alone
neither source provides a complete count of crime and both have exclusions
the crime bulletin also uses Report Fraud, police anti-social-behaviour incidents and recorded non-notifiable offences
supplementary sources have different coverage and cannot be merged without source-specific definitions
the CSEW is the most reliable indicator for long-term trends in common crimes experienced by the household population and includes unreported crimes
the reliability statement does not extend to excluded populations or very low-volume offences
CSEW estimates are subject to sampling error and non-sampling errors including recall issues
survey estimates must retain confidence intervals and quality caveats
the CSEW sample is relatively small for very low-volume crimes, making short-term estimates noisy
short-term change should not be asserted for rare offences without uncertainty checks
for crimes that are well reported and accurately recorded, police recorded crime can provide a useful picture of volume
the condition must be demonstrated for the offence before the figures are used as a trend measure
police recorded crime provides insight into demands on police and where policing effort is spent
police workload is not equivalent to underlying crime prevalence
police recorded crime can be affected by policing activity, recording practice and victims' willingness to report
changes in recorded counts cannot automatically be interpreted as changes in underlying crime
combining CSEW and police recorded crime generally gives good coverage of offences involving physical harm, loss or property damage
good coverage is not complete coverage and does not create parcel-level evidence
the CSEW includes crimes not reported to police and is widely viewed as an independent check on police figures
the survey's primary role is national estimation rather than address-level classification
responsibility for the CSEW transferred from the Home Office to ONS in April 2012
the governance change should be retained in provenance but does not itself alter crime levels
preferred measures of sexual and domestic violence come from self-completion modules and are reported separately from headline CSEW crime
interviewer-led measures are prone to under-reporting and should not replace the self-completion series
the upper age limit for self-completion modules rose from 59 to 74 in April 2017 and was removed in October 2021
time-series comparisons must retain the age-coverage changes
fraud and computer-misuse questions were added in October 2015 and first published in July 2016 after sufficient data were collected
the new questions create a documented series boundary
fraud and computer-misuse questions have been asked of the full CSEW sample since October 2017
estimates before and after the full-sample transition require comparability checks
respondents can recall incidents outside the survey reference period as if they occurred within it
telescoping can bias period-specific estimates
incidents can be omitted because respondents forget them or do not want to disclose them
non-disclosure and recall failure can produce underestimation
respondents may report that they contacted police when they did not
self-reported reporting behaviour is subject to social-desirability bias
incidents reported during interviews can be miscoded by interviewers or coders
classification outputs must retain the possibility of coding error
